name: Tarea
overview: Tarea is a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, identified in Scripture as the son of Micah. His mention is brief and primarily genealogical, with no additional notes recorded. This places him within the broader context of Israel's tribal history as preserved in the Chronicles.
namesAndTitles: The name Tarea appears in 1 Chronicles 8:35 without a given meaning. An alternate form, Tahrea, is found in 1 Chronicles 9:41 and is possibly understood as 'clever one.' Neither name is indicated as being given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Tarea is the son of Micah, establishing his immediate paternal lineage. No other family relationships are documented beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Tarea's significance lies in his inclusion in the genealogical records of the tribe of Benjamin, which underscores the faithfulness of God in preserving the lineage of His people. While not a prominent narrative figure, his mention helps maintain the continuity of Israel's tribal heritage as recorded in the Old Testament.
